data.title: Marvell Stock Price Forecast: Options Traders Expect a Large Move in MRVL Stock After Q3 Earnings
data.description:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) will announce its fiscal third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Thursday, November 26. According to TipRanks' Options Trading Tool, options traders expect a massive 11.25% move in either direction in MRVL stock in reaction to the semiconductor company's Q3 FY27 earnings. The options-implied move measures the expected size of the price change, not whether the stock will rise or fall.

Notably, Marvell stock has seen mixed reactions following earnings. Over the last four reports, shares fell 10.28% and gained 3.08%, 18.35%, and 7.87% the next day. These moves reflect an average absolute price change of 9.90%.

MRVL Stock Price Performance

Marvell Technology stock trended higher in Thursday's premarket trading after falling 2.15% to close at $145.54 on Wednesday. The premarket rebound comes as AI infrastructure sentiment gets a lift ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut following its $83 IPO pricing. Investors are also watching demand for data center connectivity and AI memory. Year-to-date, the stock has gained over 71%.

Recent Events Ahead of the Report

  • Recent developments for Marvell include its November 16 collaboration with Penguin Solutions (PENG). The two companies will work on CXL-based memory expansion and photonic optical interconnect technology for large-scale AI data centers.
  • Marvell is also preparing to acquire Lumentum (LITE) under a $115 billion all-stock deal announced on November 2. The deal aims to expand its AI connectivity business, but concerns about share dilution have weighed on the stock.

Analysts' Take on MRVL Stock

Following the Lumentum deal, TD Cowen analyst Sean O'Loughlin downgraded Marvell to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $175 from $350. O'Loughlin expects the Lumentum deal to dilute earnings per share by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2028. He also worries the deal may come near the peak of an optical market cycle. O'Loughlin said his downgrade reflects concerns about the deal's structure and timing, rather than Lumentum's business.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya also lowered its rating to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target to $225 from $400. Arya cited potential share dilution and a long regulatory process. He also noted that the deal could face customer conflicts.

Is MRVL Stock a Buy Now?

Wall Street has a Strong Buy consensus rating on Marvell Technology stock, with 24 Buys and five Holds. The average MRVL stock price target of $323.63 indicates 122% upside potential.
data.author: Shalu Saraf

data.title: Why Micron, Sandisk, and Intel Stocks Are Rallying Today, Nov. 19 — and What Wall Street Sees Next
data.description:
Chip stocks are staging a comeback in Thursday's premarket session, with Micron (NASDAQ:MU), SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) all gaining between 4% and 5%. The rebound follows weeks of heavy selling, as enthusiasm surrounding Anthropic's highly anticipated Nasdaq debut lifts sentiment toward tech companies that could benefit from the AI developer's future infrastructure investments.

Anthropic's IPO will provide the ChatGPT rival with additional capital for computing infrastructure, potentially increasing demand for advanced processors, memory chips, and data-center storage. Meanwhile, Intel has another reason to rally following encouraging news regarding its manufacturing operations.

Micron's AI Opportunity Remains Intact Despite Mounting Risks

Micron has endured a turbulent month, with the scandal surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang, concerns about excessive AI spending, and the Democrats' sweeping midterm victories weighing on semiconductor stocks. The election results have raised fears of tighter restrictions on data-center construction, potentially slowing demand for advanced memory chips. Despite these challenges, expectations for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) remain encouraging, supported by continued investment in AI infrastructure.

Nvidia's latest earnings also offered another reason to reconsider Micron's prospects. The chip giant disclosed that its supply commitments had climbed from $279 billion to $390 billion, with much of that increase related to multiyear procurement agreements. For Micron, which provides HBM components used in AI accelerators, these obligations suggest customer requirements could remain elevated.

There have also been encouraging developments regarding memory-chip pricing, with expectations of continued industry strength supporting Micron's longer-term prospects. However, legal uncertainty remains after a federal judge allowed a proposed DRAM price-fixing lawsuit involving Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron to proceed. While the allegations remain unproven, the case introduces another potential risk for investors evaluating future returns.

Despite the recent turbulence, Wall Street remains extremely bullish on Micron's longer-term prospects. MU stock boasts a Strong Buy consensus rating, supported by 28 Buys and just one Hold assigned during the past three months. The average 12-month price target of $1,624.42 suggests an upside potential of 130% from Wednesday's closing price.

SanDisk's Stock Split Arrives at a Critical Moment

SanDisk has also experienced heavy selling in recent weeks, although its latest financial results suggest underlying demand for storage products remains healthy. The company continues benefiting from data-center expansion, where customers require greater capacity to support AI applications.

In late October, the manufacturer reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.03 billion, representing a 23% increase from the preceding period. Its non-GAAP gross margin reached 85.1%, while executives projected second-quarter sales between $12.2 billion and $12.6 billion, reflecting expectations for continued customer spending.

However, concerns about a possible NAND flash memory glut have complicated the outlook for storage manufacturers. GF Securities recently warned about potential oversupply and weaker pricing, contributing to another selloff throughout the sector. SanDisk also faces longer-term competition from Chinese producers seeking greater participation in the global market.

Meanwhile, investors are preparing for the company's eight-for-one stock split, with adjusted trading scheduled to begin on November 20. Although this corporate action leaves its underlying valuation unchanged, smaller individual share prices could make ownership more accessible to retail participants.

Wall Street appears convinced that SanDisk's recent weakness has created an attractive buying opportunity, with analysts projecting 174% upside potential based on the average 12-month price target of $2,130.83. SNDK has earned a Strong Buy consensus rating, supported by 11 Buys and 3 Holds. (See SNDK stock forecast)

Intel Lands a Customer That Could Change Its Future

Intel's Thursday rally has an additional catalyst beyond the broader semiconductor recovery, following an announcement that could strengthen its long-running manufacturing turnaround.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan revealed Wednesday that the company had signed what he described as its first external customer for advanced 18A technology. The unnamed client selected Intel's 18A-P process, marking an important commercial milestone for its foundry operations.

The chipmaker also named Microsoft as the first publicly disclosed customer for its EMIB advanced packaging technology, providing another encouraging development. Their expanded relationship includes multiyear Xeon supply-capacity commitments, offering Intel another opportunity to demonstrate its competitiveness within data centers.

These announcements follow a challenging October, when disappointing fourth-quarter revenue guidance raised concerns about weakening PC demand and supply-chain constraints. Shares have lost about 39% over the past month, leaving investors eager for evidence that the turnaround strategy is delivering results.

Unlike Micron and SanDisk, Intel has yet to convince most Wall Street analysts that its recovery deserves an outright bullish recommendation. INTC stock holds a Hold consensus rating, based on 7 Buys, 25 Holds, and one Sell assigned during the past three months. Nevertheless, the average 12-month price target of $90.93 suggests a potential upside of 66% from Wednesday's closing price. (See INTC stock forecast)
data.author: Ben Yoffe

data.title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Anthropic's $81 Billion IPO Takes Center Stage
data.description:
U.S. stock futures moved higher ahead of Thursday's opening bell as investors focused on Anthropic's (ANT) highly anticipated Nasdaq debut. The maker of Claude AI is targeting a potential $1.5 trillion valuation, making it one of the largest IPOs in history.

Futures on the Nasdaq-100 (NDX), the S&P 500 Index (SPX), and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 2.07%, 1.16%, and 0.57%, respectively, as of 5:40 a.m. EST on November 19.

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share, above its initial target range of $70 to $78, following strong investor demand. The company also increased the offering size from 825 million to 980 million shares. The IPO is expected to raise approximately $81.34 billion, surpassing SpaceX's (SPCX) $75 billion June offering to become the largest IPO on record. The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement.

Meanwhile, oil prices edged higher on Thursday after falling in the previous session. Concerns about rising global oil supply and higher U.S. interest rates limited gains, while renewed geopolitical risks in the Middle East supported prices. Reports of possible further U.S. action against Iran and attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz also kept supply concerns in focus.

At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, rose 0.76% to $92.65 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 0.65% to $83.80 per barrel.

During Wednesday's regular trading session, the three major U.S. indexes closed mixed. The DJIA fell 1.11%, while the S&P 500 declined 0.23%, marking its fifth straight day of losses. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

Looking ahead, investors will also watch data on weekly jobless claims for further clues about the strength of the U.S. labor market. On the earnings front, results from Walmart (WMT), Alibaba (BABA), and Gap (GAP) are scheduled for release today. 

Global Markets

European markets traded mixed on Thursday, while Asia-Pacific markets closed mostly lower. Investors remained cautious ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, as concerns about AI valuations and the outlook for U.S. interest rates continued to weigh on sentiment.

Investors also kept an eye on the trilateral meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The talks could focus on nuclear arms control, the Ukraine war, and global security. Any progress could ease geopolitical tensions and improve investor sentiment.

Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dropped 1.95%. In China, the Shanghai Composite fell 0.28%, and the Shenzhen Component was down 1.20%. The Nikkei 225 added 0.71% and the Topix declined 0.04%.
data.author: Sheryl Sheth

data.title: Cathie Wood Loads Up on AI and Biotech Stocks, Cuts One EV Holding
data.description:
On Wednesday, Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought shares of AI and biotech companies while cutting its stake in one electric vehicle (EV) maker. According to the firm's daily fund disclosures, ARK bought shares of Kodiak AI (KDK), Twist Bioscience (TWST), Scribe Therapeutics (SCTX), and GeneDx Holdings (WGS), while selling shares of BYD (BYDDY).

On the sell side, ARK Invest sold 59,498 shares of BYD (BYDDY) through its Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ). The sale was worth about $478,958. This follows several sales over the past week, showing that ARK has continued to reduce its BYD holdings.

Wood Adds Kodiak AI Stock

ARK Invest bought 506,083 shares of Kodiak AI through its ARKQ. The purchase was worth about $551,630. ARK has previously accumulated KDK shares several times in 2026, including in April, May, and October.

Kodiak AI develops autonomous driving technology for commercial trucks and defense. In Q3 2026, the company reported revenue of $3 million, up 286% year-over-year. It posted a GAAP operating loss of $50.4 million. The figures highlight the early-stage nature of the business and the risks tied to its long-term growth plans. KDK stock is down 90% year-to-date.

Cathie Wood continues to add AI stocks focused on real-world uses. Through ARKQ, her team is betting on Kodiak's self-driving truck technology and its potential to change freight transport. However, ARK's purchases are long-term bets, and the company still has a long way to go before autonomous trucking becomes widely used.

Wood Buys More Biotech Shares

ARK Invest also bought shares of other biotech companies. Through its ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG), the fund purchased 2,835 shares of Twist Bioscience, worth about $317,520. The same ETF added 11,539 shares of Scribe Therapeutics, valued at around $181,970. This follows several recent purchases of the gene-editing company.

Separately, ARK Invest bought 4,319 shares of GeneDx Holdings through its ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK). The purchase was worth about $204,245.

Kodiak AI Stock Signals Strong Upside Ahead

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, KDK and WGS stocks have Strong Buy ratings. KDK's average price target of $8.43 implies 695% upside, while WGS's average target of $83.80 points to a potential gain of 61%.

Twist Bioscience and Scribe Therapeutics stocks have Moderate Buy ratings with potential upside of 13% and 327%, respectively.

data.title: Anthropic Gray Market Signals 24% Jump After Record $107.3 Billion IPO Beats SpaceX
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares pointed up to 24% higher in gray market trading before their Thursday debut in New York, Bloomberg reported. The early jump follows an upsized $107.3 billion IPO and private sale that beat SpaceX (SPCX) as the largest first-time share sale ever.

The stock starts trading today on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after U.S. markets open at 9:30 a.m. ET.

The Claude chatbot maker priced its stock at $83 for a $1.5 trillion value. Derivatives at IG International pointed to a 24% gain early Thursday. Crypto futures on Hyperliquid also traded near $102, or 20% above the IPO price, on over $140 million in daily volume.

Nvidia and Google Join Record $107.3 Billion Deal

Anthropic and its seven co-founders raised $107.3 billion in total, including a $26 billion private placement from backers such as Nvidia (NVDA), Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google, and AMD (AMD). Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) led the IPO with 20 other banks, regulatory filings show.

Wall Street is watching the debut after Nvidia shares fell this month following Jensen Huang's exit and AI spending worries. U.S. IPOs have dropped a weighted average of 4% this year, Bloomberg data shows. Still, Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.8% early Thursday, and Polymarket traders put 46% odds on Anthropic hitting $1.75 trillion by year-end.

"With a well-priced IPO, you always need to leave a little upside," Jacques-Aurélien Marcireau, CEO of Stilgar AM, told Bloomberg.

Anthropic Has Grown Its Revenue Run Rate to $81 Billion

More companies have been paying to use Anthropic's tools and this is what has made ANT stock an easier sell to investors. Anthropic's annual revenue run rate hit $81 billion on October 31, up $10 billion in a month, regulatory filings show. Over 11,900 customers now bring in at least $100,000 a year, up from about 1,500 in 2025.

Software developers widely use its Claude Code tool, including NASA engineers, the filings show. Anthropic is also pushing into law and healthcare, and Goldman Sachs analysts think its sales could reach about $685 billion by 2030.

Moreover, Bloomberg Intelligence estimates sales could reach $200 billion by 2028 even after 20% price cuts on some models.

Anthropic Is Facing $901 Billion in Computing Bills

Staying ahead in AI tends to come with large bills. Anthropic's spending commitments hit nearly $901 billion, mostly for chips and computing power, filings show. About $71 billion is due in the year through September 2027.

Investors should also see whether cheaper open-weight models from Chinese rivals squeeze margins. Anthropic has promised to keep Claude ad-free, and its Long-Term Benefit Trust holds power to pick or remove most board members.

"Once advertising becomes part of a company's revenue targets, the pressure to optimize for engagement tends to grow," the co-founders wrote in an investor letter in the filings. "We have chosen not to introduce that pressure into Claude."

What Is the Forecast for ANT Stock?

Four Wall Street analysts now cover ANT stock with Buy ratings, giving it a Strong Buy rating overall. The average 12-month ANT stock price target sits at $133.75.

Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes set the top target at $155, while Needham analyst Scott Berg set a $150 target. Citizens JMP analyst Patrick Walravens put his target at $125, and New Street Research analyst Pierre Ferragu set the low target at $105.

From the $83 IPO price, the average target points to about 61.1% upside. Individual targets point to gains between 26.5% and 86.7%.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: Why Are SpaceX, AMD, and Broadcom Stocks Rising in Premarket Trading Today?
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO) moved higher in premarket trading on November 19. The gains came after Anthropic  (ANT) priced its IPO above the expected range. Strong demand for the offering also lifted confidence in AI spending.

Anthropic, the maker of Claude AI, priced its shares at $83, above its initial range of $70 to $78. The offering raised $81.3 billion and valued the company at about $1.5 trillion. This made it the largest IPO on record.

The strong IPO comes as demand for Anthropic's AI models continues to grow. More businesses are using Claude for coding and other work tasks. As a result, Anthropic needs more computing power. This is creating new business for companies that supply AI chips and data center capacity.

SpaceX Has a $120.5 Billion Compute Deal With Anthropic

SpaceX has agreed to provide computing capacity to Anthropic. Under the deal, Anthropic could spend up to $120.5 billion through 2029. Monthly payments could reach about $3.1 billion once the full capacity is in place.

This makes Anthropic a major customer for SpaceX's AI compute business. The deal could also provide SpaceX with a large source of future revenue as it expands its data center capacity.

AMD Has a $5 Billion Investment Deal With Anthropic

AMD is also set to benefit from Anthropic's plans to expand its AI capacity. The two companies have agreed to deploy up to 2 gigawatts of AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs. The first deployments are expected in the first half of 2027.

AMD has also committed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic. This includes a $2.5 billion share purchase. Anthropic could spend more than $20 billion if it takes the full initial amount of AMD computing capacity.

The agreement gives AMD a larger role in supplying chips for Anthropic's AI models. It also adds to AMD's list of major AI customers.

Broadcom Benefits From Anthropic's Google TPU Deal

Broadcom is set to benefit from Anthropic's work with Aplhabet (GOOGL) on AI computing capacity. The deal will give Anthropic access to next-generation Google TPU systems, with Broadcom helping develop and supply the custom chips.

The agreement covers about 3.5 gigawatts of capacity, which is expected to come online from 2027. Broadcom also works with Google on future versions of its custom AI chips.

As Anthropic expands its use of Claude, it will need more computing power. This could support further demand for Google's TPUs and the chips Broadcom helps supply. It also gives Broadcom a chance to benefit from the growing use of custom AI chips.

Which Stock Do Analysts Prefer?

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, all three stocks carry a Strong Buy consensus rating. SpaceX has the highest implied upside at 86.59%, followed by Broadcom at 45.42% and AMD at 23.02%. All three also have high Smart Scores of 9 or 10.

data.title: Anthropic Is Set to Debut on Nasdaq Today. Defiance's 2X Daily ETFs, ANTC and ANTQ, Are Expected Monday
data.description:
Anthropic's Nasdaq Debut

Anthropic's debut comes ahead of the expected launch of two Defiance ETFs tied to its share price. The Defiance 2X ANT Long Daily ETF (Nasdaq: ANTC) and the Defiance 2X ANT Short Daily ETF (Nasdaq: ANTQ) are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. Both are single-stock ETFs with one-day objectives: ANTC seeks 200% of the daily percentage change in ANT's share price and ANTQ seeks -200%, before fees and expenses.

Anthropic made its registration statement public on October 26, set a price range of $70 to $78 a share on November 10 and kept those terms in its amended filing of November 17. The offering priced on Wednesday, November 18, at $83 a share.

The deal covers 980 million shares of Class A common stock: about 956.4 million sold by Anthropic and about 23.6 million sold by existing stockholders. The underwriters hold an option on up to 147 million more shares from the company. At the IPO price the 980 million shares are worth about $81.3 billion. Goldman Sachs (NYSE: GS) and Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) are the first of 22 underwriters named on the prospectus cover.

Seven companies have also agreed to buy $26.0 billion of non-voting Class N common stock at the IPO price in a private placement alongside the offering: Advanced Micro Devices (Nasdaq: AMD), Broadcom (Nasdaq: AVGO), Alphabet's Google (Nasdaq: GOOGL), Micron Technology (Nasdaq: MU), Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT), NVIDIA (Nasdaq: NVDA) and TSMC Partners, a subsidiary of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM).

Nasdaq has approved the Class A shares for listing, and trading is expected to open today. The opening price will be set in Nasdaq's opening auction and can differ from the IPO price.

The Company Behind the Ticker

Anthropic is the AI research lab behind Claude, which it delivers through its models, its developer platform and applications such as Claude Code. It was founded in 2021, is based in San Francisco and is organized as a Delaware public benefit corporation.

Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $33.2 billion, compared with $2.5 billion a year earlier, according to the prospectus. The third quarter alone brought in $17.0 billion. More than 11,900 customers each accounted for at least $100,000 of revenue over the prior twelve months.

The losses are also large. Anthropic reported a $1.3 billion loss from operations for the nine months and a net loss of $104.0 billion, of which $94.3 billion came from changes in the fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs. It has committed to about $900.9 billion of future spending, nearly all of it on computing capacity and infrastructure, and expects to incur about $451.6 billion of that before the end of 2030. It held $95.6 billion of cash and cash equivalents at September 30.

Voting control rests with the co-founders and a trust. Class A shares carry one vote each. A single Class F share, held by an entity of the co-founders, carries 50.1% of the voting power on general matters, and the Long-Term Benefit Trust elects a majority of the board. Nasdaq rules classify Anthropic as a controlled company.

Information about Anthropic and the other companies named is drawn from Anthropic's SEC filings and is included for illustrative purposes only. It is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Anthropic is not affiliated with Defiance ETFs, Tidal Trust II or the funds.

What ANTC and ANTQ Are Designed to Do

Defiance ETFs, a Miami-based issuer of thematic, leveraged and income ETFs, built the pair for traders who want a one-day position on ANT's share price, long or short, through a single ticker.

Each fund targets the percentage change in ANT's share price over a single day, measured from one close of regular trading to the next. ANTC seeks daily investment results, before fees and expenses, of two times (200%) that change. ANTQ seeks -2 times (-200%). On a day when ANT rises 3%, ANTC is designed to gain about 6% and ANTQ to lose about 6%, before fees, expenses and financing costs. On a day when ANT falls 3%, the results reverse.

Neither fund seeks its objective over any period longer than one trading day.

The funds do not own Anthropic stock. They get their exposure through swap agreements with financial institutions and may also use listed options, and they hold collateral such as U.S. government securities and money market funds. At or near each close, the adviser rebalances each fund so the next session starts with exposure of about 200% or -200%. Shareholders of ANTC and ANTQ have no voting rights in Anthropic and no right to any dividends it pays.

Both funds are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. Shares cannot be purchased until the funds begin trading, and the expected date may change. Once listed, each will trade like any other ETF, through a standard brokerage account.

How the Daily Reset Works

Because exposure resets every day, a fund's return over a week or a month is the compounded result of its daily returns. That result will very likely differ from 200% or -200% of ANT's return over the same period, and the difference tends to widen as volatility rises.

According to the prospectus, each fund will lose money if ANT's performance is flat over time. Each can also lose money over a period longer than a day in which ANT moves in its favor: ANTC while ANT rises, ANTQ while ANT falls.

Both funds are designed as short-term trading vehicles for knowledgeable investors who monitor their positions frequently. They are not suitable for all investors.

Inside the Funds

ANTC and ANTQ are series of Tidal Trust II and are expected to list on The Nasdaq Stock Market. Tidal Investments LLC is the investment adviser and Defiance ETFs, LLC is the fund sponsor.

Each fund charges a 0.69% management fee and estimates 0.02% of other expenses, for total annual fund operating expenses of 0.71%. That total leaves out the financing costs embedded in the funds' swap agreements, which the prospectus treats as an indirect expense.

Fund Snapshot

Fund details are from the prospectus dated November 6, 2026. The launch date is expected and subject to change.

The Bottom Line

Anthropic's shares are expected to start trading today. ANTC and ANTQ are expected to follow at 9:30 a.m. ET on Monday, November 23. One seeks 200% of the daily percentage change in ANT's share price and the other seeks -200%, before fees and expenses, and each lists total annual fund operating expenses of 0.71%. Both funds work one trading day at a time. Over longer periods their returns will very likely differ from those multiples, and either fund can lose money quickly.

Learn More About ANTC and ANTQ

The prospectus and fund details are available at defianceetfs.com/anthropic-etfs or by calling 833.333.9383.

Risks Investors Should Weigh

The objective lasts one trading day. Each fund seeks its stated multiple for a single day, measured close to close. Over longer periods, compounding means returns will very likely differ from 200% or -200% of ANT's return, and the difference widens with volatility.

A flat stock still costs money. The prospectus states that each fund will lose money if ANT's performance is flat over time. ANTC can lose money over a period longer than a day even if ANT rises, and ANTQ can lose money over such a period even if ANT falls.

One day can take the whole investment. If ANT's share price falls by more than 50% in a single trading day, ANTC investors could lose all of their money. If it rises by more than 50% in a single trading day, ANTQ investors would lose all of their money.

One company, new to public trading. Both funds depend entirely on a stock that is expected to begin trading today and has no public trading history. Newly listed shares can be highly volatile, and a halt in trading of ANT is expected to halt trading in the funds as well.

Exposure comes through derivatives. The funds use swaps and may use listed options in place of owning ANT, which adds counterparty risk. The prospectus also warns that swap and options capacity in a recently listed stock may be limited. A fund that cannot get enough exposure may miss its daily objective and may trade at wider spreads or away from net asset value.

Anthropic's risks carry through. ANT is assigned to the software industry, so both funds are concentrated there. Anthropic's own prospectus lists risks that include securing enough computing capacity, intense competition, an evolving and uncertain regulatory environment, litigation tied to its AI models, reliance on a limited number of customers and cloud providers, and a capital structure that limits the influence of Class A stockholders.

New funds. ANTC and ANTQ have no operating history. Their shares may trade above or below net asset value, and bid-ask spreads may be wider in early sessions.

For a prospectus or summary prospectus, go to defianceetfs.com/anthropic-etfs. Hard copies can be requested by calling 833.333.9383.

Investing involves risk. Principal loss is possible. The Funds seek daily leveraged (ANTC) or daily inverse leveraged (ANTQ) investment results and are intended to be used as short-term trading vehicles. They are riskier than alternatives that do not use leverage or short strategies and are not suitable for all investors. The Funds are intended only for knowledgeable investors who understand the consequences of seeking daily leveraged or daily inverse leveraged results and who will monitor their positions frequently. An investor could lose the full principal value of an investment within a single day.

As ETFs, the Funds may trade at a premium or discount to NAV. Shares are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemed from the Funds. ANTC and ANTQ are expected to begin trading on November 23, 2026. Shares cannot be purchased until the Funds begin trading, and the expected date may change.

ANT Risks. Each Fund's exposure to Anthropic (ANT) comes through swap agreements and options based on ANT's share price. Investors in the Funds have no voting rights in ANT and no right to receive dividends or other distributions from ANT. ANT has little or no public trading history, and its share price may be highly volatile. ANT's business depends on its AI models and platform, and its structure as a public benefit corporation with concentrated voting control differs from that of most public companies. Compounding and Market Volatility Risk. Each Fund has a single-day investment objective. Its performance for periods longer than one trading day will be the result of each day's returns compounded over the period, which will very likely differ from 200% (ANTC) or -200% (ANTQ) of ANT's performance for that period, before fees and expenses. Higher volatility increases this effect.

Short Sale Exposure Risk. ANTQ obtains inverse leveraged exposure through derivatives. ANTQ could lose an amount greater than its net assets if ANT's share price increases by more than 50% on a given trading day, and its investors would lose all of their money.

Derivatives and Counterparty Risk. The Funds use swap agreements and may use listed options. Derivatives may be more volatile than, and may not correlate perfectly with, the underlying security. Swap agreements expose the Funds to the risk that a counterparty will not meet its obligations.

Recent IPO and Derivatives Capacity Constraints Risk. Because ANT has little or no public trading history, the swap and options capacity available to the Funds may be limited. If a Fund cannot obtain sufficient exposure, it may not achieve its investment objective and its shares may trade at wider bid-ask spreads or at premiums or discounts to NAV.

Intra-Day Investment Risk. The Funds seek their objectives from the close of regular trading on one trading day to the close on the next. An investor who buys shares at any other time will likely have more or less than 200% or -200% exposure to ANT for the rest of that day.

Single Issuer and Software Industry Concentration Risk. Each Fund's performance depends on one company. Each Fund is also concentrated in the software industry, the industry to which ANT is assigned, and may be more volatile than a fund invested across industries.

Trading Halt Risk. Trading in ANT or in the Funds' shares may be halted. A halt may prevent a Fund from achieving its objective and may prevent investors from buying or selling shares.

Non-Diversification Risk. Each Fund is non-diversified and may be more sensitive to a single economic, business, or regulatory event than a diversified fund.

data.title: Dell and HPE Stocks Rise After Lenovo's Q2 Earnings — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares of PC maker Dell Technologies (DELL) and server manufacturer Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) rose 4% in Thursday's pre-market trading. This followed a 48% jump in Lenovo's (LNVGY) fiscal second-quarter revenue. The Chinese PC and server rival generated $30.2 billion in sales during the quarter ended September 30. This beat the LSEG consensus estimate of $27.6 billion, boosting sentiment on industry demand.

Lenovo's Q2 2027 Sales Raise Demand Hopes

According to Lenovo, its Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) division posted its best quarter on record. ISG revenue reached $11.3 billion, up 178% from a year ago.

The division handles Lenovo's AI server and storage systems business. It also provides edge computing solutions. This describes products designed to run AI locally on a device for faster response.

In addition, Lenovo's Intelligent Devices Group (IDG) revenue rose 15% year-over-year. The unit reported record second-quarter revenue of $17.4 billion. IDG makes the company's ThinkPad, Yoga, and Legion PCs. It also manufactures tablets, accessories, and Motorola smartphones.

The results show that demand for AI servers remains solid. More importantly, the earnings also show that consumers continue to buy PCs despite price increases. This matters because Lenovo is the world's largest PC maker by unit shipments.

PC makers have been forced to raise prices over the past year as memory chips and other components have become more expensive. Still, Lenovo said it widened its PC market lead over its closest rival, HP (HPQ), by 7.2 percentage points during the quarter.

data.title: Markets Brace for U.S. Jobless Claims and Factory Data After Fed Minutes Lock In Rate Hike Bets
data.description:
A new batch of U.S. economic data hits the tape on Thursday morning, led by weekly jobless claims and factory activity. Investors will be looking for clues on growth less than a day after Federal Reserve minutes cemented bets for higher interest rates next month.

The U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) held near a 19-month high around 103.82 early Thursday, while U.S. stock futures edged higher ahead of the morning releases and AI startup Anthropic's IPO. Meanwhile, spot gold (CM:XAUUSD) hovered near $3,740 an ounce after dropping to a 14-month low of $3,719.10 on Wednesday.

Jobless Claims and Factory Numbers Will Test U.S. Growth

The U.S. Department of Labor releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 a.m. ET for the week ended November 14. Economists expect 197,000 new filings, down slightly from the prior week's 200,000 print and just above the four-week average of 195,250. Weekly claims have stayed between 189,000 and 212,000 since mid-July, showing that layoffs remain low across the country.

The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia also publishes its November manufacturing index at 8:30 a.m. ET. Forecasters expect the factory gauge to come in at 20, down slightly from 20.9 in October. Around the same time, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack delivers opening remarks at the central bank's annual Financial Stability Conference.

More reports follow at 10:00 a.m. ET. The Conference Board drops its October Leading Economic Index after the gauge held flat at 99.6 in September. Existing home sales data and third-quarter U.S. Census Bureau reports on e-commerce and services spending also hit the tape at 10:00 a.m. ET.

Federal Reserve Minutes Lock In December Rate Hike Bets

Thursday's reports arrive right after minutes from the Fed's October 27–28 policy meeting reinforced a tough stance on inflation. Officials kept the benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% last month, yet nearly all policymakers backed raising rates again soon to push inflation back to 2%. Two officials even discussed a half-point hike.

"A few participants observed that inflation could prove more persistent than anticipated, in which case a shift to a more restrictive policy stance could become necessary," the Federal Open Market Committee minutes stated.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller added Wednesday that a half-point hike could be needed next month if prices keep climbing. Traders on Thursday priced in a 90% chance of a quarter-point hike and a 10% chance of a half-point increase at the December 8–9 meeting, CME Group's FedWatch tool shows.

Data released earlier this week gave rate hawks plenty of backing. Bureau of Labor Statistics figures showed October import prices jumped 1.1% for a second straight month, topping estimates for a 0.7% rise. Separate Census Bureau numbers showed October retail sales grew 0.2%, while the core control group feeding into GDP rose 0.6%.

High Mortgage Rates Drag Down Home Contracts and Permits

Housing numbers released Wednesday showed high borrowing costs are still squeezing buyers and builders, with 30-year mortgage rates holding above 7.2%. Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October from September and plunged 16.7% from a year ago to their lowest level since 2001, the National Association of Realtors reported.

"October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out," National Association of Realtors Chief Economist Lawrence Yun said.

Census Bureau construction figures painted a mixed picture for October. Housing starts jumped 9.9% on multi-family projects, though overall building permits slid 7.4%. Single-family permits dropped 8.7% to their slowest pace since May 2020.

In bond markets, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield slipped for a fourth straight session on Thursday to around 5.05%. Safe-haven buying from Middle East tensions and cheaper oil pulled yields slightly lower. West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.2% Wednesday to $83.26 a barrel after the Energy Information Administration reported a 3.4 million-barrel jump in U.S. crude stockpiles.
